title: Nonblocking feedback queue + local test recipe
content:
Quick context
- Working notes for triaging small review comments into a non-blocking feedback queue. Goal: reduce reviewer cognitive load, give authors a clear set of bite-sized followups they can patch and land quickly, and track higher-risk items separately.
- PR: #842 (backend: reduce kv-cache memory bloat on long sessions) — large-ish change, majority is allocator refactor. I was reviewer. Kept a few blocking items separate; everything below is non-blocking / can be batched.

Principles for non-blocking queue (my personal heuristic)
1) Non-functional cosmetic changes (naming, ordering) -> non-blocking. Add to queue, optionally codemod.
2) Small measurable perf improvements that don't change correctness -> non-blocking if covered by existing tests.
3) Missing logging or extra debug -> non-blocking (note where to add, but don't require for merge).
4) Any change that affects call stack/observability/compat -> blocking.
5) Security, API surface or migration-related -> blocking.

This PR: what I left non-blocking (notes to self + suggested patch snippets)
- Rename: allocate_* helpers in allocator.rs -> more descriptive names (allocate_prefix_cache -> allocate_kv_prefix). Not required to land now. Patch suggestion: simple rename with rust-analyzer refactor. Tag: small-refactor.
- Docstring expansions: several TODOs in kv_cache.rs about TTL semantics. I left inline comments. Action: author can add 1–2 sentence clarifications, link to design doc. Tag: docs.
- Tests: add an integration test that simulates interleaved short/long sessions to validate cache drop heuristics. Marked as non-blocking because unit tests cover allocator invariants; integration would be follow-up. Minimal test skeleton provided below. Tag: tests+followup.
- Logging: change debug!("evicted {} entries", n) -> trace for high-frequency code paths. Non-blocking but recommended.
- Lint: clippy suggestion (needless_collect) in helper -> file a tiny PR after merge.

Suggested local test recipe (fast, reproducible)
- env: rust 1.70, cargo, test double harness used in infra/bench.
- command: RUST_LOG=trace cargo test --test kv_cache_integration -- --nocapture
- skeleton (to copy into tests/integration/kv_cache_integration.rs):
  - spawn 3 fake sessions with different sequence lengths (5, 150, 300)
  - interleave requests to store prefix keys and then request tokens to force cache eviction logic
  - assert that long sessions keep their prefix (kv_cache.lookup(session, prefix) != None) while short sessions cycle
  - instrument memory usage by reading /proc/self/statm or using jemalloc metrics (optional)
- note: keep wall-clock under 6s for CI flakiness tolerance. If flaky, move to nightly integration job.

Batch application approach (how to actually land these non-blocking items)
- Create branch: pr-842-nonblocking-cleanups
- Run codemods for renames where trivial (rust-analyzer or sed for docs)
- Make one commit per class: renames, docs, tests, logging, lints. Keep small commit messages.
- Add GH checklist in PR description enumerating items from this document and mark as resolved as they land.

Patch sketches (copy-paste friendly)
- Rename helper (rust):
  - refactor: allocator.rs
  - from: pub fn allocate_prefix_cache(...)
  - to: pub fn allocate_kv_prefix_cache(...)
  - quick sed for occurrences: rg "allocate_prefix_cache" -n | xargs sed -i 's/allocate_prefix_cache/allocate_kv_prefix_cache/g'

- Change debug->trace
  - file: kv_cache/src/eviction.rs
  - replace: debug!("evicted {} entries", evicted) -> trace!("evicted {} entries", evicted)

Unresolved questions / followups (to either me or author)
- Q1: Are eviction thresholds policy-configurable per-customer? I left a TODO; product might want that exposed. Create infra ticket INF-1198 (linked).
- Q2: Should we add a perf-guard in CI to prevent future regressions? I suggested a tiny benchmark in cron. Follow-up: rough cron job recipe in infra/bench/notes.md.
- Q3: TTL semantics with partial-prefix updates — I flagged with \"need design sign-off\". That is blocking for correctness if we change semantics. For now, add a doc note and file an RFC.

Priority map (how to escalate)
- Merge now: PR can land after blocking items resolved (I marked 3 blocking comments in thread). Once merged, schedule a follow-up milestone for the non-blocking queue.
- Follow-up backlog (medium priority): tests, docs, logging tweaks. Estimate: 1 engineer, 1 day total if batched.
- Low priority: lints and small naming sweeps. Can be included in a maintenance sprint.

Notes-to-self (reviewer hygiene)
- When leaving non-blocking comments, include a concrete patch sample or a 2-line sed/codemod to lower friction.
- If there are >8 non-blocking items, consider grouping into a single follow-up PR; prefer many small commits in that follow-up rather than scattering 12 comments here.
- Remember to add a GH label: "followup:nonblocking" and assign to author or a maintenance lead.

Mini checklist to attach to GH comment when marking non-blocking:
- [ ] created followup branch? (pr-842-nonblocking-cleanups)
- [ ] added an integration test skeleton? (tests/integration/kv_cache_integration.rs)
- [ ] small doc note added near TTL TODOs
- [ ] created ticket for product question (INF-1198)
- [ ] created lint PR for needless_collect (optional)

Small copy of an actionable test snippet to paste in follow-up PR:

use std::time::Duration;
use my_runtime::kv::KvCache;

#[test]
fn interleaved_sessions_preserve_long_prefixes() {
    let mut cache = KvCache::new_for_tests();
    let long_id = session_id("long");
    let short_id = session_id("short");
    // warm prefixes
    cache.insert_prefix(long_id.clone(), vec![0u8; 1024]);
    cache.insert_prefix(short_id.clone(), vec![0u8; 16]);
    // simulate activity
    for _ in 0..200 {
        cache.touch_session(long_id.clone());
        if rand::random::<u8>() % 10 == 0 {
            cache.touch_session(short_id.clone());
        }
    }
    assert!(cache.lookup_prefix(&long_id).is_some());
}

Final: keep this doc pinned to PR thread until follow-ups are scheduled. If author prefers, I can open the follow-up branch and land the trivial renames.

-- Imran
